props.title: Nepali weddings, planned from the first tika to the bidai
props.text: We plan Hindu weddings in the Kathmandu valley, Nagarkot, Dhulikhel and Pokhara: the purohit, the janti, the mandap, the kitchen and the thousand small things in between, so both families can simply be there.

image.alt: Strings of marigold and white jasmine hanging as a curtain at a bride’s home

props.eyebrow: Now planning for Mangsir, Magh and Falgun · Sanepa, Lalitpur

props.quote: A Nepali wedding is four days, two families, one purohit and a kitchen that never closes. Our job is to make sure the bride’s mother gets to sit down.
props.name: Pratiksha Joshi

items.title: The rituals, done properly
items.text: We work with your family purohit, or introduce one. The sait is fixed first; then the samagri for every ritual is bought, checked and laid out before the family arrives, down to the last supari and the sagun for each guest.

image.alt: A woman in a yellow sari and flower jewellery beside marigold strings

items.title: Mehndi and haldi at home
items.text: Marigold strings, low seating, a dhol player and a mehndi artist for the women of the family. We arrange it in your courtyard or on the roof, and clear it away before the wedding morning.

image.alt: A white floral mandap at the end of an aisle, with hills behind

items.text: Party palaces in the valley, a garden in Dhulikhel or a lakeside hotel in Pokhara. We design the mandap, the stage and the entrance, and we are on site from the first delivery to the last chair.

items.a: For Mangsir, Magh and Falgun, four to six months ahead; party palaces fill first. For other months, two to three months is usually enough.

items.q: Do you plan Newar, Brahmin and Chhetri weddings?
items.a: Yes, and mixed ones. The rituals differ from family to family, so we always sit with the elders and the purohit before writing the schedule.

items.q: Can you work with our own caterer or decorator?
items.a: Yes. We coordinate them as we would our own, and we do not charge them a commission.

items.q: Do you plan weddings outside the valley?
items.a: In Nagarkot, Dhulikhel, Chitwan and Pokhara. Travel and rooms for our team are added at cost.
30% to book, 40% a month before, and the rest after the reception. Bank transfer or cheque, with a VAT bill.

pages.title: Planning
pages.seoTitle: Wedding planning services · Janti Weddings, Lalitpur
pages.seoDescription: Sait and rituals, venue, catering, decor, janti and guests: what we arrange for a Nepali wedding, and the six months to the bidai.

props.title: Wedding planning, all of it or part of it
props.text: From fixing the sait with your purohit to the last chair folded after the reception. Choose the parts your family needs.

image.alt: A Nepali bride in red holding a bouquet and smiling

props.eyebrow: Hindu weddings across the valley and beyond

items.title: Sait and rituals
items.text: Working with your purohit on dates, times and the samagri for each ritual. A printed schedule for both families.

items.title: Venue
items.text: Party palaces, hotels and gardens. We visit with you, check parking, generators and kitchens, and negotiate the rate.

items.title: Catering
items.text: A tasting with two or three caterers. Menus priced per plate; we count plates on the night.

items.title: Decor
items.text: Mandap, stage, entrance, marigold for the house and the car for the bidai.

items.title: Janti
items.text: Cars, band baja and the route, timed so the janti arrives on the sait.

items.title: Photography and make-up
items.text: We introduce people we trust and put them on the timeline. You book and pay them directly.

items.title: Guests
items.text: Invitation cards, the guest list, SMS reminders and hotel rooms for relatives from outside the valley.

items.title: On the day
items.text: Four coordinators with a timeline, an emergency kit, spare safety pins and everyone’s phone number.

image.alt: A bride and groom seated before the fire at their wedding rites

props.caption: The rites at the mandap, with the purohit and both families close by.

items.title: First meeting and the sait
items.text: We meet both families, fix the date with the purohit and write the budget.

items.title: Venue and caterer
items.text: Visits, a tasting and the advance paid.

items.title: Decor and invitations
items.text: Mandap design approved, cards printed, guest list started.

items.title: The schedule
items.text: A minute-by-minute plan for each day, shared with every vendor and both families.

items.title: We move in
items.text: Deliveries, set-up, rehearsal with the purohit, and four days on site.

items.q: We have a family decorator already.
items.a: Good. We share the schedule with them and make sure the mandap is ready before the purohit arrives.

items.q: How many people will we deal with?
items.a: One planner from the first meeting to the reception, and three more coordinators during the week.

items.q: Do you handle the reception too?
items.a: Yes, in the Full planning package, or on its own as a one-day job.

props.title: Start with an hour
props.text: The first meeting is free, at your home or our office in Sanepa.

props.heading: What is not in our fee
props.body:
The venue, food and drinks, decor materials and flowers, the purohit’s dakshina, photographers, make-up and transport are paid by you, directly or through us at cost.

We never take a commission from a venue, a caterer or a decorator. When we recommend someone, it is because they turned up on time the last ten weddings.

pages.title: The wedding week
pages.seoTitle: A Nepali wedding week, day by day · Janti Weddings
pages.seoDescription: Mehndi, haldi, purbanga, janti, swagat, kanyadan, sindoor, bidai and reception: how a four-day wedding runs with us.

props.title: How a wedding week runs with us
props.text: Four days, written down to the minute and shared with both families, the purohit and every vendor.

image.alt: A bride and groom sitting cross-legged side by side during the rites

props.eyebrow: A typical four-day Hindu wedding in the valley

items.title: Mehndi at the bride’s home
items.text: Seating and marigold set up by 15:00. Mehndi artists for the bride and guests; dhol from 18:00; dinner at 19:30.

items.title: Haldi
items.text: Turmeric for the bride and groom at their own homes. We clear up by 11:00.

items.title: Purbanga puja
items.text: With the purohit, at both homes. Samagri laid out the night before.

items.title: Janti leaves
items.text: Cars and band baja at the groom’s gate. We call ahead so the swagat is ready.

items.title: Swagat and jaimala
items.text: The groom is welcomed with fruit, flowers and tika; garlands are exchanged at the mandap.

items.title: Kanyadan, sindoor and pote
items.text: At the mandap with the purohit. We keep the elders seated and the photographers out of the smoke.

items.title: Bidai
items.text: The bride leaves in the decorated car. Our team stays to pack up the venue.

items.title: Reception
items.text: Guests arrive; the couple takes the stage at 19:00; dinner from 19:30.
